Let $z = \dfrac{1967 + 1686isin\theta}{7 - 3icos\theta}$ is a positive integer.

$⇒ z = \dfrac{1967 \times 7 - 1686 \times 3sin\thetacos\theta + i\left(1686 \times 7sin\theta + 1967 \times 3cos\theta\right)}{49 + 9\cos^{2}\theta}$

Now taking imaginary part as zero we get,

$1686 \times 7sin\theta + 1967 \times 3cos\theta = 0$

$⇒ \left(281 \times 6\right) \times 7sin\theta + \left(281 \times 7\right) \times 3cos\theta = 0$

$⇒ 42sin\theta + 21cos\theta = 0$

$⇒ tan\theta = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \cos^{2}\theta = \dfrac{4}{5} \text{ and } sin\thetacos\theta = - \dfrac{2}{5}$

$⇒ z = \dfrac{281\left(49 + \dfrac{36}{5}\right)}{\left(49 + \dfrac{36}{5}\right)} = 281$

Hence, the value of $n$ is $281$

Match each entry in List-I to the correct entries in List-II.

List-I List-II
$\left(P\right)$ ${\left|z\right|}^{2}$ is equal to $\left(1\right)$ $12$
$\left(Q\right)$ ${\left|z - \overset{¯}{z}\right|}^{2}$ is equal to $\left(2\right)$ $4$
$\left(R\right)$ ${\left|z\right|}^{2} + {\left|z + \overset{¯}{z}\right|}^{2}$ is equal to $\left(3\right)$ $8$
$\left(S\right)$ ${\left|z + 1\right|}^{2}$ is equal to $\left(4\right)$ $10$
$\left(5\right)$ $7$

The correct option is
questions.solution:
Given,

${\left|z\right|}^{3} + 2{z}^{2} + 4\overset{¯}{z} - 8 = 0 . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now on taking conjugate both side we get,

${\left|z\right|}^{3} + 2\overset{¯}{z}2 + 4z - 8 = 0 . . . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

$\left\{\text{Note}\left|\overset{¯}{z}\right| = \left|z\right|\right\}$

Now subtracting both equations we get,

$2\left({z}^{2} - \overset{¯}{z}2\right) + 4\left(\overset{¯}{z} - z\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(z - \overset{¯}{z}\right)\left[2\left(z + \overset{¯}{z}\right) - 4\right] = 0$

$∵ z = \overset{¯}{z}$ (not possible) or $4x = 4 ⇒ x = 1$ $\left\{\text{as}z + \overset{¯}{z} = 2x\right\}$

So, $z = 1 + \lambdai$

$⇒ \left|z\right| = \sqrt{1 + {\lambda}^{2}} \text{ and } \overset{¯}{z} = 1 - \lambdai$

Now putting the value of $z, \left|z\right| \text{ and } \overset{¯}{z}$ in given equation we get,

${\left(1 + {\lambda}^{2}\right)}^{3 / 2} + 2\left(1 - {\lambda}^{2} + 2\lambdai\right) + 4\left(1 - \lambdai\right) - 8 = 0$

$⇒ {\left(1 + {\lambda}^{2}\right)}^{3 / 2} + 2\left(1 - {\lambda}^{2}\right) = 4$

$⇒ {\left(1 + {\lambda}^{2}\right)}^{3 / 2} = 2\left(1 + {\lambda}^{2}\right)$

$⇒ \left(1 + {\lambda}^{2}\right)\left[\sqrt{1 + {\lambda}^{2}} - 2\right] = 0$

$⇒ {\lambda}^{2} = 3$

Now solving,

$\left(P\right)$ ${\left|z\right|}^{2} = 1 + {\lambda}^{2} = 1 + 3 = 4$

$\left(Q\right)$ ${\left|z - \overset{¯}{z}\right|}^{2} = {\left|1 + \lambdai - \left(1 - \lambdai\right)\right|}^{2} = {\left|2\lambdai\right|}^{2} = 4{\lambda}^{2} = 12$

$\left(R\right)$ ${\left|z\right|}^{2} + {\left|z + \overset{¯}{z}\right|}^{2} = 4 + {\left|\left(1 + \lambdai\right) + \left(1 - \lambdai\right)\right|}^{2} = 4 + 4 = 8$

$\left(S\right)$ ${\left|z + 1\right|}^{2} = {\left|1 + \lambdai + 1\right|}^{2} = 4 + {\lambda}^{2} = 4 + 3 = 7$

$∴ P \to \left(2\right), Q \to \left(1\right), R \to \left(3\right), S \to \left(5\right)$

options:
a line not passing through the origin

$|z|=\sqrt{2}$

the Y-axis

Let $z=\cos \theta+i \sin \theta \begin{aligned}\frac{z}{1-z^2}$& =$\frac{\cos \theta+i \sin \theta}{1-(\cos 2 \theta+i \sin 2 \theta)}$\\
& =$\frac{\cos \theta+i \sin \theta}{2 \sin ^2 \theta-2 i \sin \theta \cos \theta}$\\
& =$\frac{\cos \theta+i \sin \theta}{-2 i \sin \theta(\cos \theta+i \sin \theta)}$\\
& =$\frac{i}{2 \sin \theta}

Let $z_1=\frac{w-\bar{w}_z}{1-z}$, be purely real.
$ \begin{array}{rlrl}
\Rightarrow & z_1 & =\bar{z}_1 \\
& \therefore & \frac{w-\bar{w} z}{1-z} & =\frac{\bar{w}-w \bar{z}}{1-\bar{z}} \\
\Rightarrow & & w-w \bar{z}-\bar{w} z+\bar{w} z \cdot \bar{z} & =\bar{w}-z \bar{w}-w \bar{z}+w z \cdot \bar{z} \\
